Here's a story that happened a last Monday on my train.

 

First a little background information, I'm 19, study Biotechnology and live about 1.5 hours away from my school, half of that journey I spend in a crowded train, the rest is bus, metro and my bicycle.

I was coming back from a day in the lab, it was 6:30 in the afternoon and I'll readily admit that I was tired. We get one lab day in each week and they're full, often with the whole class working until the building closes.

My train stops in front of me, Dutch trains have a little area with fold up chair along the walls next to the doors before the main seating area in between the doors starts, this is also where the majority of the standing passengers will stand if the train is full. I take one of the folding chairs, happy that I got a place to sit. the two other chairs were quickly taken by an older lady and a businessman. A couple more students enter and lean against the walls close to the doors (when the doors close they too have an (uncomfortable) place to sit on).

Then I hear huffing and puffing outside. One of the standing students, I'll call him Pete moves to assist whoever has trouble entering but very quickly leans back after getting a better look at what's standing at the door. I don't blame him, his love for his intact spine is probably bigger then his pity.

Finally something big enters the train, this thing had a lot of trouble with dragging its body up the steps of the carriage door and needs to take a few seconds to catch its breath, allowing me to take a closer look. I conclude that at birth this thing must have been female, but I no longer think that the term is appropriate, "it" will have to do.

After about 10 seconds of wheezing in awkward silence the thing looks at her surroundings, and sees that there are no seats free here. First she tries her best to give me an evil eye, I meet her gaze and remain unmoved. Her head slowly tilts to look at the businessmen, for a moment I fear that he would give in but I had severely underestimated him, their eyes lock and he smirks in her face. Victory. It almost looks as if the ham would speak up but instead she turns to look at the older lady, she doesn't seem to acknowledge its presence.

The thing moves further into the train, probably hoping to find a free chair in the actual seating area, a quest I know to be impossible at this time unless two people give up their seats for the ham. As the door closes behind the cow. Pete chuckles, as do the two other students. "That's a first" I truthfully say, 19 years of living in the Netherlands and I've never seen anything like this, the thing must have been almost twice my weight and I'm almost 2 meters (6'6) tall. "For me too." agrees the older lady.

The doors close and Pete and his girlfriend sit down. The businessman takes out his newspaper, I take my headphones and lab journal from my bag. I start going through my notes and start working while the experiments are still fresh on my mind.

But alas, the door to the rest of the carriage opens again after a few minutes, and the thing waddles back as expected there were no free seats further into the train. Instead of trying for seats in the other direction as we all probably hoped she leans against the wall instead. I try my best to ignore her as I continue to do my work but slowly her smell becomes more apparent.

Ten minutes after the train has started moving Pete has had enough, he takes a can of deodorant out of his bag and sprays his armpits with enough Axe to clear the hambeast's smell. Speaking of the beast, is is visibly having trouble with remaining upright, just as I start to wonder if it's going to make it to the station she decides to sit down on the ground. The thing: "Are you a doctor?"

The thing: "But are you a medical student?"

The thing: "I know you are." Wheeze "A lot of people have a fear of doctors, it is very inconsiderate of you to not take their feelings into consideration."

Finally the root of all evil is revealed, it gestures towards my bag. I had left it open after getting my headphones and notes, this left my lab coat visible.

Me: "That lab coat, not a doctors coat."

Me: "It has smileys, notes and rainbows drawn on it, I don't think that's very appropriate in a hospital setting.

It continues staring at me. I close the bag and try to focus on my work again. Luckily it doesn't speak up again and I escape from the train at the next station.
